chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Being the only Black man in club-date bands; Bill Dillard
summary: He was hired because he could entertain as well as play, alongside Bill Dillard, and had earlier played with white musicians like Zoot Sims and Al Cohn.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You mentioned, when you were playing you were often the only--you say--"colored person" in the band...

Yeah, well that was because I could entertain. You see what I mean? Well, they knew I could play the music...I had to know the music, but I could entertain too. So that was doin' two for one. I was doin' a double.
How much would those gigs pay?
Union scale. Yeah. If you were a sub-leader then you got a little more, you see. You were in charge of the job, you know.
Up to this time...I mean you mention there being white bands---up to this time, the bands you'd played in, had they all been Black bands?

Well, I had played with white musicians, you know, all through those years, you know, but...I played with this alto...um... this clarinet player that died, he used to be with Hamp, oh what was his name...anyway, I played with him at the Apollo Theater. And then, you know,

Zoot and I and Al Cohn and this alto player that used to be with Lenny Tristano. You know, we were all friends, you know, and we'd jam on 52nd Street and I knew the guys all through the years, but this was the first actual situation where I was exposed to a whole new facet of the music business. And there was one other colored fellow who knew all the music. He'd sing in Yiddish and do everything. His name was Bill Dillard and he was also an actor--but he was a top man. And we became friends, you know. But he and I were usually the only colored dudes to be hired on those jobs, at that particular time, because--for the simple reason--because on these jobs, you know, you got to entertain. You got to play the music, but you got to entertain too, you know what I mean: make people happy. A lot of time people spend so much money for a wedding or an anniversary or somethin' like that and it's a package deal and so the band's got to be on the ball, you know. So everybody in the band..each guy..had his own thing, whatever he did, and this one did this, and did that and the other, but the main thing is to
put on a show, you know.
